Text Message Scams

Nationwide Scam Text UK: Spot a Fake Building Society SMS

Nationwide scam texts are designed to look urgent and legitimate—but one wrong click can hand over your bank details and money.

By Alex Bacsa · Published 2026-05-19 · Updated 2026-08-01 · 7 min read

Quick answer: Treat a Nationwide text asking you to log in through its link as a scam. A message asking you to claim, confirm or release the 2026 Fairer Share payment is also fake because there was no claim process. Send suspicious messages to phishing@nationwide.co.uk, forward texts to 7726, and use Call Checker if a caller follows up.
Key rule: verify through an official route you opened yourself, not the link, number, app, or payment details supplied by the suspicious message.

Being targeted right now? Do this

  1. Stop. Don’t pay, transfer money, or share passwords, PINs, or one-time codes.
  2. Contact your bank on the number on the back of your card if your money or details may be at risk.
  3. Use the right recovery route. Follow the payment, account and identity checklist; reporting differs in Scotland.

Check before you pay, not after

The most useful thing Nationwide offers a member staring at a suspicious text is used before any money moves. Its Scam Checker Service invites you to run a payment past staff first — the wording on nationwide.co.uk is to talk to the society if you are unsure about a payment you are about to make, and it will look into it.

The freephone line published on the Scam Protection Promise page runs 24 hours a day, seven days a week, branch staff will do the same review in person, and the service covers payments set up through the app, the Internet Bank and Open Banking.

The Scam Protection Promise is attached to that conversation and inseparable from it. If you talked to Nationwide through Scam Checker before making the payment, and it did not tell you not to proceed, it says it will give you back every penny should the payment turn out to be a scam. It is not an after-the-event refund guarantee for a payment you made without asking. The Promise applies to Faster Payments, CHAPS and electronic transfers between Nationwide accounts.

Card payments, cash withdrawals, cheques and overseas payments sent by SWIFT or SEPA fall outside it, and Nationwide says it may change or withdraw the Promise, telling members in branch and on its website if it does.

That pre-payment conversation is precisely what an urgent SMS is designed to rush you past.

Call Checker: proving who is on the line

Since January 2026 the Nationwide banking app has carried Call Checker, which answers a question 159 cannot. Dialling 159 reaches the society on a line you opened yourself; it tells you nothing about the person already talking to you. Call Checker does exactly that.

Stay on the call, open the app, go to More and pick the Call Checker tile. The screen states either that you are on a call with a named Nationwide colleague or that you are not on a call with the society. If it says the second thing, the caller is impersonating Nationwide, no matter how much they appear to know about your accounts.

Nationwide launched the tool because impersonation runs through so much of the fraud its members report, and a scam text is very often the reconnaissance step for that call.

Four things Nationwide will never ask a member to do

The society publishes a short list. It will never ask you to:

  • Give it your full one-time code or card reader code.
  • Transfer your money to a safe account.
  • Log into the Internet Bank through a link in an email, text or social media message.
  • Use, re-enable or re-sync your card reader over the phone.

The third entry decides most texts on its own. A message telling you to sign in through its link is requesting the one thing Nationwide states it never requests.

Member-shaped bait: Fairer Share and restriction warnings

Membership hands fraudsters hooks a high-street bank cannot offer. The Fairer Share Payment is the obvious one: in 2026 more than four million eligible members received £100 between 10 and 30 June, paid automatically into an open Nationwide current account, with nothing to apply for.

Because no application or claim process exists, the fraudulent discriminator is a request to do something with the payment. A message asking you to claim it, confirm your details for it, sign in to receive it or release it is invented — for example Nationwide: your Fairer Share payment could not be processed. Confirm your details: nationwide-member.example. A text that merely links to genuine Fairer Share information is not, by itself, proof of fraud; it is the demand for an action on your side that gives it away.

The other family leans on loss instead of reward: unusual activity, a restriction about to be applied, a card about to be stopped. Both want the same outcome, which is you signing in somewhere that is not the society's own app.

Open that app and look for yourself. Your genuine balance, your genuine payment history and any action Nationwide actually needs from you all appear there, and no real restriction is ever lifted by completing a web form you arrived at from an SMS.

Reporting it as a member

Nationwide asks members to send suspicious emails, texts and messages to phishing@nationwide.co.uk. It does not reply to each one, but it says it reviews what arrives, and the detail helps shut down the infrastructure behind a campaign. Forward the SMS to 7726 as well so your mobile network sees the sender, and pass an emailed version to the NCSC at report@phishing.gov.uk.

Where money has actually gone, or you have given away enough for someone to impersonate you, add a police record: Report Fraud takes reports at reportfraud.police.uk and on 0300 123 2040, while in Scotland that report goes to Police Scotland on 101 instead.

If you have already replied, tapped or paid

Ring the society immediately. Its 24-hour fraud number is published in the app, on nationwide.co.uk and on the back of your card. 159 routes participating callers to Nationwide — Stop Scams UK describes the service as connecting customers of more than 99% of UK retail bank current accounts, which is not a guarantee for every handset or network, so use the published number if 159 does not connect for you. Say which of three things happened: you entered credentials, you approved a one-time code, or you sent a payment. They trigger different responses inside the society.

Nationwide's Scam Protection Promise may apply only if you used its Scam Checker and talked to the society before making the covered payment, and it did not tell you not to proceed. Separately, the mandatory reimbursement rules may apply to eligible Faster Payments or CHAPS transfers made from 7 October 2024. Those rules cap an eligible claim at £85,000 and allow 13 months from the payment to raise a case, and they are conditional every time rather than automatic.

While a claim is open, work through the payment, account and identity actions in our scam recovery checklist.

Frequently asked questions

Where is Call Checker in the Nationwide app?

Stay on the call, open the banking app, tap More and choose the Call Checker tile. It has been available since January 2026 and shows either that you are on a call with a named Nationwide colleague or that you are not on a call with the society.

I got a text about my Fairer Share payment — can it be genuine?

Not one that asks you to claim it, confirm details for it, sign in for it or release it. Nationwide pays Fairer Share automatically into an open current account; the 2026 payment of £100 landed between 10 and 30 June with no application process. A message that only links to genuine information is not by itself proof of fraud — the request for an action from you is.

Does the Scam Protection Promise guarantee my money back?

Nationwide says it will refund every penny of a covered scam payment if you talked to it through Scam Checker before paying and it did not tell you not to proceed. The Promise covers Faster Payments, CHAPS and electronic transfers between Nationwide accounts; listed exclusions include cards, cash, cheques and SWIFT/SEPA payments. Nationwide may change or withdraw the Promise.

Would Nationwide ever ask me to move money to a safe account?

Never. It sits on the society's published list of things it will never ask a member to do, alongside handing over a full one-time code, signing in through a link, and re-syncing a card reader over the phone.

Where do I report a Nationwide scam text?

Send it to phishing@nationwide.co.uk and forward it to 7726. If a payment left your account, ring the society's 24-hour fraud line or 159 first, then log the case with Report Fraud — Police Scotland on 101 if you are in Scotland.

Fast checks

  • Pause before sending money or credentials
  • Verify with an official site, app, or number
  • Never share one-time passcodes
  • Be sceptical of bank transfer pressure
